result.note: Tests the IOCL–Mauritius fuel supply deal, the MAHASAGAR doctrine's origin and India's refining position.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) signed a long-term agreement to supply fuel to Mauritius. Consider the following statements about it:
items: IOCL replaces Mauritius's State Trading Corporation as the importer of fuel into Mauritius.
The agreement locks in roughly 750,000 tonnes of annual demand for five years.
It is India's first such long-term fuel supply deal outside South Asia.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because Mauritius's State Trading Corporation remains the importer. IOCL becomes the sole supplier under a Sales and Purchase Agreement tied to a government-to-government MoU, which replaces STC's old competitive tenders.
questions.source: Mauritius's State Trading Corporation (STC) remains the importer, but the new Sales and Purchase Agreement, tied to a government-to-government MoU, locks in roughly 750,000 tonnes of annual demand for five years, replacing STC's old competitive tenders.

questions.prompt: MAHASAGAR, India's Indian Ocean doctrine, was unveiled in March 2025 in which country?
questions.explain: MAHASAGAR was unveiled in Mauritius in March 2025. The August 2026 fuel deal, together with a 27,500-tonne bunker-fuel facility at Port Louis and a joint biofuels policy, sits under this doctrine.
questions.source: It all sits under MAHASAGAR, India's Indian Ocean doctrine, unveiled in Mauritius in March 2025.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's petroleum refining sector, as reported in August 2026:
items: India imports nearly 90% of the crude oil it refines.
India's refineries produce more fuel than the country consumes, making it a net exporter of refined products.
India already supplies the full fuel requirements of Nepal and Bhutan.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. India's 23 refineries produced 267 million tonnes, and exports of refined products reached roughly 61.4 million tonnes in FY 2025-26, which allowed India to keep supplying Nepal and Bhutan in full even through the West Asia crisis.
questions.source: Its 23 refineries produced 267 million tonnes last year, more than it consumes, making India a net exporter: exports reached roughly 61.4 million tonnes in FY 2025-26.
